clients.name: Rossi Family
clients.liquidity: Maintain a three-tier liquidity reserve designed to cover at least 36 months of essential family requirements.
clients.objectives: Long-term real capital growth|Maintain family liquidity and resilience|Diversify across public and private markets
clients.priorities: Maintain the 36-month liquidity framework|Rebalance the financial portfolio annually|Develop the alternatives and succession-planning structures
clients.summary: A fictional Italian family with a €20m net worth, previous UK links and two adult children. The case allocates €10m of investable assets across €5m of public markets and €5m of alternatives, while maintaining a €1.38m three-tier liquidity reserve and coordinating direct real estate with future succession and wealth-planning structures.

scenarios.name: Ordinary Italian taxation
scenarios.description: Italian residents are modelled on worldwide income. Progressive IRPEF applies to work and rental income; investment income uses the relevant 26% or qualifying 12.5% assumption. UK tax on London rent is credited where available.

scenarios.name: Historical Impatriati · 2022 relocation

featureCards.title: London rental property
featureCards.text: UK source taxation remains relevant. Ordinary and Impatriati scenarios model an Italian foreign tax credit; Art. 24-bis does not credit UK tax against the fixed substitute tax.

featureCards.title: Legacy UK Stocks & Shares ISA
featureCards.text: The ISA may retain UK tax relief after emigration, but it is not automatically tax-free in Italy. No income or gain is invented: the model stays at €0 until realised data are available.

featureCards.title: Italian BTP
featureCards.text: The contractual coupon is included. A 12.5% qualifying sovereign rate is assumed in all three scenarios.

featureCards.title: Foreign sovereign bonds
featureCards.text: Contractual coupons are included. The 12.5% Italian rate is a modelling assumption subject to issuer eligibility; source-country withholding is TBD.

featureCards.title: Public-market investments
featureCards.text: Accumulating ETF NAV growth is performance, not annual taxable cash income. Distributions and realised disposals enter only when a taxable event and source are known.

sensitivity.note: Each cell shows the lowest-tax regime and annual tax. Foreign investment income is an additional 26%-taxable modelling variable; all other base assumptions are held constant.

sources.title: Historical Impatriati regime
sources.note: Eligibility and historical relief for workers who transferred residence to Italy. The 2022 case must be reviewed under the rules then in force.

sources.title: Option for new residents
sources.note: Official option and instructions for the foreign-income substitute tax. The model uses the historical €100k amount relevant to a 2022 entrant.

sources.title: IRPEF rate bands
sources.note: Modelled progressive rates: 23% to €28k, 35% from €28k to €50k and 43% above €50k.

sources.title: IVIE rate
sources.note: The dashboard uses a 1.06% IVIE assumption on a €1.9m proxy value for the London property.

sources.title: ISAs when moving abroad
sources.note: A legacy ISA can generally remain open with UK tax relief, but contributions normally stop while non-UK resident. Italian treatment is separate.

sources.title: UK rental income for non-residents
sources.note: UK rental income remains within the UK tax system, including the Non-resident Landlord Scheme.

sources.title: Taxed twice on foreign income
sources.note: Foreign tax relief depends on treaty rules and the income item. The dashboard credit is a model assumption, not an entitlement conclusion.

sources.title: Personal Allowance for non-residents
sources.note: The UK rental calculation assumes entitlement to the £12,570 Personal Allowance; this must be confirmed.

sources.title: Income Tax rates and allowances
sources.note: The model uses the £37,700 basic-rate band and 20% rate for the illustrated UK rental calculation.

sources.title: Italian investment taxation assumptions
sources.note: 26% for general financial income and realised gains, subject to instrument classification and transaction facts.

sources.title: Qualifying sovereign assumption
sources.note: 12.5% is applied to the BTP and listed foreign sovereign coupons only as a modelling assumption; eligibility requires instrument-level confirmation.

sources.title: Trust and structuring perimeter
sources.note: Future trust income is deliberately excluded until Pillar 3 identifies the settlor, beneficiaries, assets, jurisdiction and tax residence.
